messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Figure size and mysterious \maxwidth
parts:
I see a discussion about \maxwidth on github but couldn't understand it.

I'm getting emitted code from the latest knitr on CRAN like this: {\centering \includegraphics[width=\maxwidth]{gen-rcscomp} 

after using <<rcscomp,mfrow=c(1,2),h=4,w=5,cap='Restricted cubic spline component variables for $k = 5$ and knots at $X = .05, .275, .5, .725$, and $.95$. The left panel is a $y$--magnification of the right panel.  Fitted functions such as those in Figure \\ref{fig:gen-rcsex} will be linear combinations of these basis functions as long as knots are at the same locations used here.',scap='Restricted cubic spline component variables for 5 knots'>>=

after defining

render_listings()
unlink('messages.txt') # Start fresh with each run
hook_log = function(x, options) cat(x, file='messages.txt', append=TRUE)
knit_hooks$set(warning = hook_log, message = hook_log)# , error = hook_lst_bf)
knit_hooks$set(par=function(before, options, envir)
               if(before && options$fig.show != 'none')
               {
                 p <- c('bty','mfrow','ps','bot','top','left','rt','lwd',
                        'mgp','tcl', 'axes')
                 pars <- opts_current$get(p)
                 pars <- pars[!is.na(names(pars))]
                 if(length(pars)) do.call('spar', pars) else spar()
               })
opts_knit$set(aliases=c(h='fig.height', w='fig.width',
                cap='fig.cap', scap='fig.scap'))
opts_knit$set(eval.after = c('fig.cap','fig.scap'))

\SweaveOpts{fig.path='gen-', fig.align='center', w=4.5, h=3.5, fig.show='hold', fig.lp='fig:gen-', fig.pos='htbp', par=TRUE, tidy=FALSE}

\maxwidth is undefined ; any help appreciated.

Thanks
Frank

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Figure size and mysterious \maxwidth
parts:
Hmm... I cannot reproduce the problem with the latest version on CRAN.
In theory knitr should define \maxwidth in the LaTeX preamble. Anyway,
I think the problem should go away with opts_chunk$set(out.width =
NULL).

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
<<setup, include=FALSE>>=
render_listings()
# opts_chunk$set(out.width = NULL)
@

<<>>=
plot(1)
@
\end{document}

Regards,
Yihui
